source.title: In-Context Examples Suppress Scientific Knowledge Recall in LLMs
source.authors: Chaemi Jang; Woojin Park; H. Yun; Dong-Man Lee; Ji Hee Kim

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites work on induction heads in its related-work section but does not test or rely on induction heads. Its experiments concern scientific knowledge recall and strategy use under in-context examples, not induction-head formation, token-index loss, or training-time transitions.
record.gate_note: The only induction-head-specific statement is a citation to prior work. The scientific-task accuracy and strategy-classification results below concern a related but different ICL behavior; they do not measure any claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper mentions induction heads once, citing Olsson et al. 2022 in related work. Its experiments measure scientific-task accuracy and chain-of-thought strategy shares in API models under 0-shot versus 10-shot prompting. It does not identify, ablate or track induction heads, does not measure loss by token index, and does not study training dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also stress three points: the displacement is direction-consistent across domains; recall is triggered by domain vocabulary (semantic decoy test); and the results hold across four models, with hidden-state and logit evidence in 7–8B open models.
record.recipe_differences: No induction-head method or original-claim procedure is applied.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scientific-task outcomes vary by domain and number of examples; the paper also tests prompting interventions. These settings do not test the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: 10-shot same-formula examples cut the Parametric strategy share by 6–20pp in all five domains for GPT-5.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context examples displace knowledge-driven derivation toward example-driven fitting on scientific latent-structure tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: The accuracy effect of 10-shot examples varies by domain: Economics −15.7pp, Chemistry −6.2pp, Physics +0.2pp, Biology +1.3pp, Geoscience +13.3pp. The signs for Economics and Geoscience replicate across four models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The accuracy consequence of in-context examples on scientific tasks depends on how the displaced strategy compares with the one that replaces it.

record.problems: The authors note that their behavioral strategy evidence relies partly on chain-of-thought classification, which may not faithfully reflect internal computation. They also note that the representational models are smaller than the primary GPT-5.2 model and that their benchmark uses canonical textbook tasks.
record.rows_left_out: No induction-head-specific results were reported. Other scientific-task analyses and model replications were omitted because they do not measure an aspect of the claim versions.

untested.parts: No identification of induction heads or of previous-token-head composition.
No training-time analysis, loss curves or formation window.
No attribution of in-context learning to induction heads; no loss-by-token-index measure.
No search for induction heads across models or architectures.
Training data and training setup are not varied; only the prompt examples change.
Few-shot behaviour is not attributed to any head or mechanism. The paper explicitly says it lacks mechanistic evidence.

record.verdict_notes: The extracted rows correctly carry versions ['none']. This is a behavioural ICL study; its only link to induction heads is a citation, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Does not identify, intervene on, or measure induction heads or previous-token-head composition.
Does not study training-time formation, training loss curves, or token-index in-context learning gains.
Does not measure induction heads as a mechanism for most in-context learning or loss by token index.
Does not test induction behavior across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
Varies examples and task domains, but does not test whether induction heads form or persist depending on data and training setup.
Does not compare induction heads with other mechanisms for few-shot task learning.
Does not study the stages or transitions of induction-head formation.
